01 / NATIONAL PRIORITIES

Intelligence that advances Saudi Arabia’s environmental goals.

Water efficiency, restoration survival and environmental resilience require a clearer picture of conditions on the ground—and a faster path from evidence to authorized action.

Conserve water

Identify irrigation needs, stress conditions and opportunities for more targeted intervention.

Sustain greening

Monitor establishment, vegetation health and restoration performance over time.

Extend field reach

Employ autonomous aircraft and converted helicopters for inspections and approved logistics.

02 / INTEGRATED CAPABILITY

From observation to measurable action.

The proposed EMYRGEN Climate Intelligence Network brings environmental data, mission intelligence, autonomous aviation and operational decision-making into one coordinated Saudi capability.

01

Observe

Satellite, weather, ground and environmental measurements.

02

Understand

Geospatial analysis, anomaly screening and mission priorities.

03

Inspect

Autonomous sensing missions with appropriate aircraft classes.

04

Act

Authorized ground response, precision operations and equipment logistics.

05

Verify

Follow-up measurement, evidence packages and environmental results.

Saudi-controlled mission governance, technical teams and local support underpin each stage.
03 / THREE AUTONOMOUS AVIATION TECHNOLOGIES

Three aircraft classes. One national mission system.

Each EMYRGEN aviation technology addresses a distinct requirement—from precision inspection and regional sensing to autonomous helicopter conversion and environmental logistics.

Precision sensing

EGX-10

Light autonomous VTOL aircraft for planting-site inspection, vegetation imaging, irrigation assessment and localized missions.

10 kg reference payload · electric / hybrid variants
Regional intelligence

EGX-200

Medium autonomous VTOL platform proposed for extended regional surveys, environmental observation and specialized scientific sensors.

200 kg reference payload · up to 6 h reference endurance
Autonomous logistics and intervention

Helicopter-to-UAS Conversion

EMYRGEN transforms existing manned helicopters into autonomous aircraft to support equipment delivery, remote operations and industrial capability.

Payload and endurance depend on the selected converted airframe
Aircraft specifications and proposed Saudi mission configurations require platform-specific engineering, approvals and validation.
04 / WATER INTELLIGENCE

Better water decisions start with better information.

Integrated environmental observations can help Saudi operators prioritize irrigation, identify drought stress and evaluate the efficiency of restoration programs.

Identify priority inspection areas

Compare site observations with ground measurements to identify potential water stress and direct follow-up inspection where it can improve decisions.

05 / SAUDI GREEN INITIATIVE

Protect the investment behind every planted tree.

Environmental restoration delivers lasting value when vegetation survives, water is used efficiently and results can be independently assessed.

Vegetation health

Identify stress, disease indicators and declining canopy condition.

Water efficiency

Support irrigation decisions informed by site conditions.

Verified survival

Compare establishment and survival at 6, 12 and 24 months.

07 / HELICOPTER-TO-UAS CONVERSION

Autonomous heavy-aircraft capability built from existing helicopters.

Through helicopter-to-UAS conversion, EMYRGEN proposes to extend Saudi field capability beyond sensing to autonomous transport of equipment, restoration supplies and approved mission payloads.

The logistics scene illustrates a proposed mission; the engineering and flight photographs show aircraft-conversion source material. The targeted 1,000–3,000 kg class remains airframe- and configuration-dependent.
Equipment delivery

Transport pumps, irrigation components and scientific equipment to selected operating areas.

Remote operations

Support restoration teams where terrain or distance complicates land access.

Saudi localization

Develop conversion engineering, integration, maintenance and operational expertise within the Kingdom.

08 / CLOUD INTELLIGENCE

Aerial atmospheric intelligence for Saudi research.

Environmental sensing aircraft can complement satellite observations, ground instruments and weather radar to support atmospheric study and authorized rain-enhancement research.

Atmospheric sensing

Humidity, aerosol and cloud-condition measurement packages.

Scientific integration

Link airborne measurements with satellite and radar observations.

Validated methods

Support Saudi research institutions through approved missions and scientifically assessed findings.

09 / SANDSTORM & DESERTIFICATION INTELLIGENCE

Understand dust-source conditions. Strengthen environmental resilience.

By combining satellite context, soil exposure, vegetation observations and airborne measurements, Saudi operators can better prioritize local erosion assessments and forecasting support.

Source screening

Identify candidate areas of bare soil or vegetation loss.

Field measurement

Gather targeted observations to strengthen environmental understanding.

Local mitigation

Assess suitable stabilization and land-management measures.

11 / NATIONAL IMPACT & SAUDI TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT

Measure what matters—and build the capability locally.

The program would be evaluated through ecological outcomes, operating efficiency and the depth of Saudi technical capability, not aircraft flight hours alone.

Tree survival

Verified survival at six, twelve and twenty-four months.

Water per surviving tree

Water-use intensity linked to genuine restoration outcomes.

Time to assessment

Elapsed time between anomaly identification and validated review.

Restoration coverage

Hectares surveyed, revisited and independently verified.

Cost per treated site

Intervention cost and comparison with ground alternatives.

Saudi capability

Local engineers, operators, maintenance and analytics teams.

SAUDI-BASED ENGINEERING

Localization is part of the commercial proposition.

A Saudi operating model would connect aircraft conversion, sensor integration, environmental data management, engineering, training and maintenance under negotiated industrial and technology agreements.

12 / PILOT PROGRAM & PARTNERSHIP

A phased path from demonstration to Saudi national capability.

The proposed first decision is to establish a joint Saudi–EMYRGEN technical and commercial working group to define a funded pilot program, beginning with water security, vegetation health and autonomous environmental operations.

Months 0–3

Prepare & demonstrate

Define Saudi partners, mission requirements, candidate sites, permissions, baseline measurements and pilot budget.

Months 4–12

Water & Green Initiative

Conduct authorized missions, evaluate irrigation optimization and measure restoration outcomes.

Year 2

Expand capability

Validate converted-helicopter logistics use cases and extend atmospheric and dust intelligence.

Year 3+

Scale what works

Expand independently validated applications with Saudi technical support and industrial participation.

STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIP PROPOSAL

From environmental intelligence to measurable national results.

Establish a joint Saudi–EMYRGEN technical and commercial working group to define and launch the Saudi Climate Intelligence Pilot Program.
